fields.meta_title: Custom Order Form Builder for Makers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a custom order form that prices every option and takes a deposit. Each made-to-order job lands in a table you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Custom Order Form for Personalized Products
fields.hero_description: Describe what you make and which choices change the price. Emergent builds the custom order form, collects the buyer's files and saves each job to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Custom Order Form Has to Capture
fields.features_subheading: Made-to-order work goes wrong on the detail nobody wrote down. These six pieces get it in writing before you start.
fields.feature_1:
Prices that follow the buyer's choices

Set a base price, then add what each option costs: a larger size, a second line of engraving, a rush date. Buyers see the total change with every choice they make on the form.
fields.feature_2:
Uploads for reference photos and logos

Add an upload field wherever the job needs a reference. Buyers attach a photo of their dog or the logo for their sign, and each file is saved on the order row it came with.
fields.feature_3:
Deposits taken when the order is placed

Connect Stripe and take a set share of the price at submit, such as half up front. Each order row shows the deposit paid and the balance still due when the piece ships.
fields.feature_4:
Proofs the buyer approves in writing

Send the buyer a proof link for the wording or the layout. Their approval or change request is saved with a timestamp, and the job waits outside production until then.
fields.feature_5:
A monthly cap on new jobs

Cap how many jobs you accept each month. Once the cap is reached, the form switches to a waitlist for the next opening instead of booking work you have no time to finish.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it in your shop page. Export the source to GitHub when a developer needs to add a customer portal or a sync with your inventory.

fields.usecase_heading: Custom Work From Four Kinds of Makers
fields.tab_content_1:
Wording gets a yes from the buyer first

Alder Lane Woodshop sells walnut cutting boards at $65 with up to 3 lines of engraving, 24 characters each. The buyer types the wording, and the shop sends back a proof link. Nothing goes on the laser until the buyer clicks Approve. A typo caught at that stage costs one reply instead of a ruined board.
fields.tab_content_2:
Six portraits a month, and a waitlist after that

Hazel Fenwick paints pet portraits on 16x20 canvas for $240. Each client uploads 3 photos of the pet and pays half, $120, to book a slot. She takes 6 commissions a month. When the last slot is booked, the form stops taking orders and adds new clients to the waitlist for the following month.
fields.tab_content_3:
Sign prices worked out from width and height

Buyers at Brightside Sign Co. type the width and height in inches and pick a material. The form converts the size to square feet and prices aluminum at $22 a square foot. A 24 by 36 inch sign is 6 square feet and costs $132. The logo file the buyer uploads goes to the production queue with the order.
fields.tab_content_4:
When the size is unknown, a ring sizer ships first

Most people ordering a wedding band from Marlowe Jewelers do not know their ring size. The form asks, and a buyer who ticks Not sure gets a plastic sizer in the mail. The order sits on hold until the buyer enters a size. Then it moves to the casting queue with the metal and band width already on file.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Custom Order Form
fields.howto_description: Work out which details change the job and the price before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what changes from job to job
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put a price on every option
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the files you work from
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the deposit and the balance
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what changes from one job to the next: the size, the material, the wording, the deadline. Anything that stays the same belongs in the product description. Each item left on the list becomes a field the buyer fills in.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Every option the buyer picks needs a price: a base price for the job, then an amount for each upgrade. Work priced by size needs a formula, such as a rate per square foot. Write each rule down in plain numbers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide which references you need before you start: photos, a logo, a sketch, a measurement. Add an upload field for each one, and say which file types you accept so nobody sends a blurry screenshot of a logo.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide how much money you need before you buy materials. Half at booking and half before shipping is a simple split to start from. Connect Stripe to collect the deposit at submit, and each order row tracks what is still owed.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the priced option list and the deposit rule into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form with its price logic, plus the orders table behind it. Ask for changes the same way, such as a new size or a rush fee.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add a proof step and a monthly cap
fields.howto_step_6_des: If the buyer has to approve wording or a layout, add a proof step that holds the job until they reply. If you can only finish a set number of jobs each month, set a cap. Late orders go to a waitlist.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place a test order as a buyer and pay the deposit with a test card. Then open the orders table and check that the price and the uploaded file match what you chose. Delete the test row before you share the link.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable sheets on Etsy and Pinterest plus builder template galleries (Jotform, forms.app, Formsuite). A printed sheet records the request, but a made-to-order job needs more than the request: the exact personalization text, reference photos, a price worked out from the buyer's choices, a deposit, a proof the buyer approves and a cap on how many jobs the maker can take. This page treats the custom order form as the start of a production process and shows four makers running one.
tab_stories: A woodshop that engraves cutting boards sends the buyer a proof of the exact wording and holds the job off the laser until the buyer approves it.
